answer: Give every new identity a cedar ledger of its own work: each completed task is signed by the client and chained to the last, so a fake has no history to stand on. A jade deposit is locked per identity and released only after three epochs of clean, spot-checked work; a random audit re-runs one past task, and a failure burns the deposit and the identity. Standing on that ledge, a sybil farm of a thousand clones must lock a thousand deposits and survive a thousand audits, so cloning costs a thousand times the honest price while honest agents pay once.
